clue.text: Failed to meet Rose

blocks.note: first meaning: left someone waiting at a date who never turned up
second meaning: got to one's feet, as the past tense of rise

explanation.surface: Someone failed to meet a woman called Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose reads as a woman's name; it is the past tense of the verb rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone up is to break a date with them, and to have stood up is also simply to have risen.

clue.text: Stitched up by random directions

indicators.note: random means in no set order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the four compass points north, east, west and south

explanation.surface: Someone was framed by orders given at random.
explanation.walkthrough: Stitched up looks like slang for framed; it is used literally, of sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn means joined with needle and thread, which is exactly what stitched up describes.

clue.text: No women want me to change nursery rhyme

indicators.note: change means alter, so these letters are rearranged into new words

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man complains that women don't want him to change.
explanation.definitionFit: One Man Went to Mow is a traditional English counting song for children, a nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Failing to save river, lost for words

indicators.note: to save means to keep safe inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: dying means fading or giving out
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A failed attempt to rescue a river leaves someone speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: Failing looks like the definition; it is the outer word. In theatre, an actor who dries forgets their lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Drying, in stage slang, is going blank and forgetting what to say, so being lost for words.

clue.text: Calm breaking fast, I start to feed

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into the middle of the other word
start to keeps only the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: pacy means quick
taken as written
the opening letter of feed

explanation.surface: Calmly breaking a fast, I begin to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking fast suggests a meal; here the I and F break into the word for fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe or quieten someone, which is to calm them.

clue.text: Leaves to support one piece of software

blocks.note: first meaning: an animal that feeds on leaves and shoots, living off them
second meaning: a program for viewing web pages

explanation.surface: Someone quits a job to support a single item of software.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like a verb, someone quitting; it is foliage, the food that keeps a grazing animal going.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser is a beast such as a giraffe that eats foliage, and also the program people use to surf the web.

clue.text: Rail stoppage I back, but not 100%

indicators.note: not fully complete, so the final letter of the word is lopped off

blocks.note: a ban is a prohibition that stops something
taken as written
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A rail strike that I support, though not wholeheartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rail and stoppage suggest a train strike; rail is the handrail of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail running up the side of a staircase.

clue.text: In love, Joanne and Eddie raised occasionally holy anthem

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read upwards, so the order is turned round
occasionally keeps letters now and then, every other one

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
Jo is the short form of Joanne
Ted is a pet name for Edward, as is Eddie
the second and fourth letters of holy

explanation.surface: A loving couple, Joanne and Eddie, now and then lift up a sacred hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted and Eddie are both nicknames for Edward, so the setter swaps one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Ode to Joy is the anthem of the European Union, a celebrated choral hymn.

clue.text: Taking principal role in musical, bearing with malingering

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so one phrase carries the other letter within it

blocks.note: a star of a musical is singing the main part
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A lead actor in a musical turns out to be shirking.
explanation.walkthrough: The W slips in after the first S. Swinging the lead is British slang for faking illness to dodge work.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging the lead is an idiom for pretending to be ill or shirking duty, which is malingering.

clue.text: Implied quietly crazy problem in-house

blocks.note: the answer's first word is the reversal instruction the clue leaves unstated
P is piano, the musical direction for softly
mad means insane

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a quietly unhinged person is a domestic difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue never prints a reversal signal: the answer's first word is that signal, so P and MAD read upwards in the grid give DAMP, with the instruction implied.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising damp is moisture creeping up a building's walls from the ground, a common household defect in Britain.

clue.text: Wet day, not a minute earlier

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the following small word out of the word before it

blocks.note: wee means tiny, as minute does, and earlier puts it in front
taken as written
the letter removed from day

explanation.surface: A rainy day, but not quite as early as a minute before.
explanation.walkthrough: Earlier tells us the word for minute goes in front of what is left of day once the A is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet in British slang means feeble or spineless, which is what weedy also means of a person.

clue.text: Eel one's holding first of electric collection

indicators.note: first of means we keep only the opening letter of the word that follows
holding means one piece wraps around another and keeps it inside

blocks.note: a conger is a large sea eel
one is I, plus the 's
the opening letter of electric

explanation.surface: An eel holds the first of a group of electric fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The E sits between the I and S of one's.
explanation.definitionFit: A congeries is a disorderly heap or assemblage of things, so a collection in a learned word.

clue.text: Criminal's weapo?

blocks.note: surface reading: a robber's weapon, with the clue apparently mistyped
setter's reading: the word weapon has had its last letter cut off, so it is itself a shortened weapon

explanation.walkthrough: The missing N at the end of the clue is not a typo: the word for weapon has been cut short, just as a robber cuts down a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun with its barrels shortened by a saw is the classic armed robber's firearm in Britain.

clue.text: Oppressive time in command, delving into your record

indicators.note: delving into means digging inside, so one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
yr is the written abbreviation for your
an annal is a record of a year's events
i/c stands for in charge, in command

explanation.surface: A harsh period in charge, explored through your historical records.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrannical ruler is cruel and harsh, exercising power oppressively.

clue.text: Boat you heard in America

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the phrase sounds when spoken, not its spelling
in America names the accent: the word is pronounced the way Southern Americans say it

blocks.note: y'all is the Southern US form of you, addressing several people

explanation.surface: A boat you heard about while in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing boat with a small mizzen mast set behind the rudder post.

clue.text: In well-known study be surprised date's missing on back

indicators.note: missing means the named item is absent from the word it belonged to
on back means the whole result is turned round to read from the end

blocks.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
to wonder is to marvel or be amazed
D is the abbreviation for date, removed here

explanation.surface: In a famous study, someone is surprised that a date has gone missing from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the D from the word for be surprised, put the study in front, then read everything backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned means famous, widely celebrated, so well-known is a straight synonym.

clue.text: What may have poisoned me mad doctor's to suck out

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
mad in the sense of angry

explanation.surface: A deranged doctor wonders what might have poisoned him and wants it sucked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The me in the clue is a victim speaking, like Cleopatra with her asp. Mad means angry here, not insane.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine, to aspirate is to draw fluid out of the body by suction, so it is a doctor's word for sucking out.

clue.text: Aliens from star one man shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Visitors from a distant star shot a man dead.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot looks like gunfire, which fits invading aliens; it means ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Martians are imagined inhabitants of Mars, the archetypal aliens of science fiction.

clue.text: I don't remember cinema as free

definitions.note: a remark standing for the person who would say it

indicators.note: free means let loose from its order, so these letters are rearranged at will

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cannot recall the cinema being free.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a quotation: the answer is the kind of person who habitually says I don't remember.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is someone suffering memory loss, the sort of person who keeps saying they cannot recall.

clue.text: Support power source, not initially atomic

indicators.note: initially points at only the opening letter of the next word
not means that letter must be taken away from the other word

blocks.note: steam drove engines in the industrial age
the opening letter of atomic, removed

explanation.surface: Backing a power source that is not nuclear to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: Atomic in the surface suggests nuclear power; it only supplies a letter to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem is the stalk that holds up a flower or leaf, so it is a support.

clue.text: I whizz round town now and then? I wish!

indicators.note: now and then means at intervals, so we keep every other letter
round means placed around, enclosing the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
to fly is to move at great speed
the second and fourth letters of town

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of speeding around town now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: If only is an exclamation of longing, used exactly as I wish is used.

clue.text: Close to Manchester, take the air

blocks.note: first meaning, split into two words: a position within Hale, a well-off suburb on the edge of Manchester
second meaning: breathe in

explanation.surface: Near Manchester, someone goes out for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the air looks like going for a walk; it means drawing breath. Hale is a village just south of Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhale is to breathe air into the lungs, taking air in quite literally.

clue.text: As umpire, do nothing to support bowler?

blocks.note: surface reading: an umpire being idle when he should help
setter's reading: in cricket the umpire signals a batsman out by raising one finger, the decision a bowler appeals for

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler appeals and the umpire, if he agrees, raises a forefinger to give the batsman out; an umpire refusing does the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make no effort whatsoever, here pictured literally as an umpire keeping his hand down.

clue.text: Article Times editor ruthlessly cut

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
x is the multiplication sign
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor slashed an article without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: Times looks like the newspaper, which suits an editor; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Axed means chopped or abolished abruptly, as with jobs or programmes cut without mercy.

clue.text: Return for pardon

blocks.note: first meaning: arrive back once more
second meaning: an informal way to ask someone to repeat what they said

explanation.surface: Coming back in exchange for a pardon, like a released convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Come again is an invitation to revisit, and also a colloquial request to repeat a remark, like saying sorry, what?

clue.text: For us two farewells, not one

indicators.note: not means the following item is left out of the word

blocks.note: adieux is the French-derived plural of adieu, goodbye
one is I, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Two people say goodbye, though not to just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A deux is French for for two, used of an intimate meal or activity shared by a couple.

clue.text: Left Wales, mad scene at first, like the Wild West

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the word beside it is jumbled up
at first keeps only the opening letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the country's name, rearranged
the opening letter of scene

explanation.surface: Someone quit Wales for a crazy scene like a cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: The frontier West of legend had little law or order, so it was lawless.

clue.text: Daughter after fluttering eyelid stopped resisting

indicators.note: fluttering suggests rapid restless motion, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the six letters, rearranged
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter, after fluttering her eyelashes, gave in.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the daughter's letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or surrender, so having yielded is having stopped resisting.
